items.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: And I met him later on in my career, yeah.

ctx.x: Quincy Jones went there. But anyway he talked about that and he says if he had his choices he would go to Berklee, or to Schillinger House. So somehow that stayed in my head. I said well I think I’ll go up and try it. And so after we were discharged and working with this monster pianist for six months I decided to give that a shot. But prior to leaving the military again, I was talking to this piano player Oscar about Ray Brown. I says, “you know this Ray Brown guy?” And of course we’d been listening to Shearing…

and all that and Oscar, those were the two major pianists at the time. He says, “yeah, I’ve heard of Ray Brown.” And he says, “there’s a guy down in Miami can do everything Ray can do.” I says, “who is that?” He says, “Sam Jones.” I didn’t know who Sam Jones was. I’d never heard of him. And later on he was working with Cannonball and quite a few others. And I met him later on in my career, yeah. Anyway I get out of the military and decide that I’d try to go back to Vero Beach. I went to Vero Beach and got a job…
